clue.text: Move apart, see?

indicators.note: to move the letters is to shift them about, so the words that follow get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone demonstrates splitting things up and asks if you follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges APART and SEE together; the whole clue also describes the answer, since moving apart is what parting does.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide or part company is to go off in different directions from one another.

clue.text: Fall on to floor from bench

explanation.surface: Something tumbles off a seat onto the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Sediment settles when it sinks to the bottom; a settle is also a high-backed wooden bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Particles sinking to the bottom of a liquid is one verb sense; the other is a long wooden seat with arms.

clue.text: Force ten, perhaps, out to sea?

definitions.text: Force ten, perhaps, out to sea?

parts.words: Force ten, perhaps, out to sea?
parts.note: reads like a gale warning, but describes a naval squad that compelled men, ten of them perhaps, into service at sea

explanation.surface: A storm of the highest strength is reported offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force ten' looks like the Beaufort scale; here 'force' is a verb and 'ten' a number of men.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, naval recruiters seized civilians and forced them aboard ships as sailors.

clue.text: Author did a bit of jogging

parts.note: did, of jogging, means ran
a bit of means some

explanation.surface: A writer took a little exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did a bit of jogging' reads as 'ran some'; Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was an English writer of children's adventure novels.

clue.text: Unexpected plot development for title character

explanation.surface: A writer looks for a surprise ending suited to the hero of the book.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is the title character of the Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise turn in a story is one sense; the other is Dickens's orphan hero, named in his novel's title.

clue.text: Complain having leader replaced by article that's feeble

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter, which is swapped for another piece

parts.note: to complain is to object
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone whines about a newspaper piece that is weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having leader replaced by' swaps the opening O of OBJECT for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject means wretched and spiritless, hence weak or pitiful.

clue.text: Crammed with packages of threatening appearance?

definitions.text: Crammed with packages of threatening appearance?

parts.words: Crammed with packages of threatening appearance?
parts.note: read as a compound, the word suggests a place stuffed with bundles of hay, while meaning menacing

explanation.surface: A storeroom stuffed with parcels looks menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the word looks like 'bale-full', full of bales; really it means menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleful describes a look that is menacing or full of malice.

clue.text: Fodder plant may sound novel

indicators.note: signals that the word must be said out loud and matched by its sound

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: The name of a crop resembles a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent EMMA and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmer is an ancient kind of wheat, grown for grain and animal feed.

clue.text: I stock up, even going in for a style of cooking

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'I stock up, even going in for a style of cooking': TANDOOR (an oven) plus I is plain, but no parse of 'stock up' and 'even' gives the letters; probably an OCR misread ('even' for 'oven'?) that the held text cannot confirm.
annotationWithheld.clue: I stock up, even going in for a style of cooking

clue.text: Woman has success, even though bloody

parts.note: to have success is to win
if can mean even though, as in 'pleasant, if dull'
something bloody is red

explanation.surface: A woman triumphs despite being hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Winifred is a woman's given name.

clue.text: I can't see who this story's about

definitions.text: I can't see who this story's about

parts.words: I can't see who this story's about
parts.note: a reader complaining of an unclear story, or literally a tale whose hero cannot be seen

explanation.surface: A reader is baffled about the protagonist of a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: H. G. Wells's novel is about a man nobody can see.
explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells's novel concerns a scientist who makes himself unseeable.

clue.text: Wildly attack hooligan about consequences of fire …

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, so it is placed outside

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
ash is what remains after a fire

explanation.surface: A yob runs amok over the aftermath of a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildly attack' looks like it might signal an anagram, but it is the definition, and 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out violently or verbally without restraint is the phrasal verb's sense.

clue.text: … blaze appearing to conclude almost immediately

parts.note: to conclude something from evidence is to infer it

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: immediately means now

explanation.surface: A fire is about to end any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the W of NOW, leaving NO.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, raging fire.

clue.text: Fearsome animal has hair to tear out

parts.note: a mane is a long growth of hair

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are out of place and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A frightening beast pulls its hair out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEAR to ATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is a predator, such as a tiger, that attacks people.

clue.text: In academic period, son knocked out piece of verse

indicators.note: a piece knocked out of a word is removed from it

parts.note: a trimester is an academic term
s is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: During term a boy was floored by a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimeter is a line of verse with three metrical feet.

clue.text: One has favourite line, bowling

parts.note: in cricket an over is a spell of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A cricketer has a pet line of attack in the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adores a particular person has a darling, a cherished sweetheart.

clue.text: Parasites finally removed by cat in shade

indicators.note: the final letter is taken away

parts.note: vermin are pests and parasites
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: Fleas are got rid of by a cat lying in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally removed' drops the N at the end of VERMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermilion is a brilliant red colour.

clue.text: Given new order, turned to

explanation.surface: Things were rearranged and someone took up a new course.
explanation.walkthrough: Re-sorted means sorted again; 'resorted to' means turned to.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorted a second time is one sense; the other is having had recourse to something.

clue.text: A bit of work, getting back to problem with cereal

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of work in physics

indicators.note: getting back means the following word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A small job, returning to a grain problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' reverses TO to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease affecting rye and other grain crops.

clue.text: Nearly all football team showing talent? That's fairly arguable

parts.note: a football side is eleven, so nearly all of it is ten
an able person shows talent

explanation.surface: Most of a talented football side is a reasonable proposition.
explanation.walkthrough: A football team has eleven players; nearly all is ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be defended or maintained in argument.

clue.text: Hard work extremely rarely ends in turmoil

parts.note: the selected letters ends with in, which is taken as written to open the answer
dust, as in kicking up a dust, is a commotion

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Hard work very seldom finishes in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' keeps only the outside letters of 'rarely', which come last; 'ends in' tells you what precedes them. 'Turmoil' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym, as in a dust-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means diligence and steady hard effort.

clue.text: One swallowed by watery grave

indicators.note: a piece swallowed by another ends up inside it

parts.note: serous means watery, like serum
i is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone drowns in a watery tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed by' puts I inside SEROUS. 'Grave' looks like a noun here, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious both mean solemn or weighty.

clue.text: In lake, a gallon's inadequate

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: In a lake, one gallon of water isn't enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or insufficient in amount.

clue.text: Aggressive action taken by one. insulted

explanation.surface: Someone who has been insulted lashes out.
explanation.walkthrough: An offence is an attack; one who is insulted takes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Attack, as opposed to defence, is one sense; the other is the feeling of hurt when insulted.

clue.text: In meal, two couples drink litre

indicators.note: to drink something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: two couples are four

explanation.surface: Two pairs at dinner down a litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' puts L inside FOUR. Meal here is ground grain, not a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is coarsely ground grain, and flour is finely ground grain.

clue.text: Bad weather going past country and heading east — towards here?

definitions.text: Bad weather going past country and heading east — towards here?

indicators.note: going past places one piece after the other

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom
rain is bad weather

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Rain clouds pass over Britain and move east, towards a country there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' takes the opening letter of 'east'. Read whole, the clue pictures weather drifting east from Britain towards the country named.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a country in eastern Europe, lying east of Britain.

clue.text: Old teacher using a couple of pronouns

parts.note: us is a pronoun
her is another pronoun

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned schoolmaster uses a pair of pronouns.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher was formerly an assistant master at a school.

clue.text: Solving problem incompetent has at gallery?

explanation.surface: A bad shot struggles at a shooting gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Troubleshooting is fixing faults; an incompetent at a shooting gallery has trouble shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing and fixing faults is one sense; the other, read as two words, is difficulty in hitting targets.

clue.text: Where Hardy strode around?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about where the novelist Thomas Hardy went walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges STRODE. Thomas Hardy set his novels in Dorset, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is the English county where Thomas Hardy lived and set his Wessex novels.

clue.text: Bearing offering, finally refused by church

indicators.note: the final letter is refused, so it is dropped

parts.note: a present is an offering
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A gift is turned down in the end by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally refused' drops the last T of PRESENT. Bearing here means demeanour, not direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence is impressive bearing or poise.
